clue.text: Paper required — the first edition

indicators.note: the first letter of the word the is taken, as the clue says plainly

parts.note: an edition of a magazine is an issue

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the first printing of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' asks for the first letter of 'the', T; 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin, soft kind of paper, as in tissue paper used for wrapping.

clue.text: Move to continue the football game or concede defeat

definitions.text: Move to continue the football game

explanation.surface: A footballer restarts play, or gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: A restart from the touchline in football is taken by hand; to give up is to throw in the towel.

clue.text: Settled, or prepared to fight

explanation.surface: An account was paid, or two people raised their fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying off a debt is to square it; adopting a boxer's stance to face an opponent is the other sense.

clue.text: Take off some weight?

parts.note: suggests dieting to lose pounds, but means removing cargo or a burden from a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about slimming down.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'weight' is not body weight but a load.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge cargo from a lorry or ship removes a heavy burden.

clue.text: Opens up route passing through mountains

indicators.note: a route passing through mountains sits inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a route

explanation.surface: A new road through the mountains opens up access.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain (Ben Nevis), so mountains are BENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to open it up, extending its scope.

clue.text: Government measure

explanation.surface: A state's policy or yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is governance by a state, and a ruler is a measuring stick.

clue.text: Acclaim new papal practice

indicators.note: new suggests something made afresh, so the letters of the word papal are rearranged

parts.note: use is a practice or custom

explanation.surface: Praise greets a novel custom from the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PAPAL into APPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is public acclaim or approval.

clue.text: Spot-on old-time variety performance

parts.note: ex means former, from an older time
an act is a turn in a variety show

explanation.surface: A music hall turn from the past is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: A variety show is a British music-hall entertainment of separate acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on means precisely correct.

clue.text: Colonist gets letters sent out

indicators.note: letters sent out are dispatched in every direction, here their own letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pioneer receives post that has been posted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges LETTERS; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who has moved to make a home in a new land.

clue.text: Problem doesn't start with foreign currency

indicators.note: a word that does not start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: trouble is a problem

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises with money from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' must first become its synonym TROUBLE; 'doesn't start' then removes its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the monetary unit of Russia, a currency foreign to British readers.

clue.text: One always remembers the penal settlement

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'One always remembers the penal settlement', gives only 'One always remembers' for an elephant; 'the penal settlement' has no reading for this answer and a search of the exact text finds nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: One always remembers the penal settlement

clue.text: Sort of study carried out by bathyscope?

definitions.text: Sort of study carried out by bathyscope?

parts.words: Sort of study carried out by bathyscope?
parts.note: a deep-sea diving vessel literally explores far below the surface, like a thorough examination

explanation.surface: A scientist asks what research a submersible does.
explanation.walkthrough: A bathyscope (bathyscaphe) is a deep-sea submersible; a thorough study is literally one far down.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough, detailed study is described with this phrase about depth.

clue.text: Feature film put on before the big fight

definitions.text: Feature film put on before the big fight

parts.words: Feature film put on before the big fight
parts.note: read not as a cinema film but as a coat applied to the facial features before going into battle

explanation.surface: A movie is screened before a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature film' suggests cinema, but here features are the face and the film is a thin coating; the big fight is a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors traditionally daubed colours on their faces before battle, a coating meant to frighten foes.

clue.text: Association distributing claret

indicators.note: distributing spreads things about, so the letters of the wine word are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A society hands out red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributing' rearranges CLARET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms in league to fix prices, a commercial alliance.

clue.text: Rose terminated the sitting

explanation.surface: Someone got up and so ended the session.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to one's feet is to rise; ending a period of sitting means getting upright.

clue.text: Artist's model who barely earns a living

definitions.text: Artist's model who barely earns a living

parts.words: Artist's model who barely earns a living
parts.note: barely sounds like scraping by on little money, but means wearing nothing while posing

explanation.surface: A poorly paid life model scrapes a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean 'only just', but it means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Life models often pose unclothed for artists.

clue.text: If one doesn't enter it one's pulled through

definitions.text: If one doesn't enter it one's pulled through

parts.words: If one doesn't enter it one's pulled through
parts.note: pictures a gravely ill patient at the threshold of dying who recovers instead of crossing over

explanation.surface: A doorway riddle: fail to go in and you are dragged through anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: To be pulled through is to recover from serious illness; someone at this threshold who does not cross it survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Being near to dying is described as lying at this metaphorical doorway.

clue.text: Flying — up and down the touchline?

explanation.surface: A winger runs along the sideline at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds aloft are in flight; a winger in football or rugby plays along the side of the pitch.

clue.text: He kills a coiuple of fools in the end

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the word for fools appears twice in a row

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone finally murders two idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple of' doubles ASS; 'in' gives IN as written, and 'the end' is a link-like finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer or murderer of public figures is a person who kills.

clue.text: Work on site can cause obstruction

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: Building work on a site can block the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' as OP (opus) is a crossword convention; 'on' just means placed next to, and 'can cause' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance, a hindrance put in someone's way.

clue.text: Loose bones scattered around the church

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the church abbreviation
scattered bones lie in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Bones lie strewn about a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like the opposite of tight, but here means morally lax; the CE convention stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose here means immoral or indecent, like lewd talk.

clue.text: Big name in the performing arts

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, here the letters perform tricks and change order

explanation.surface: A celebrity in theatre and music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing arts' looks like one phrase, but 'performing' rearranges ARTS; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity, someone famous, is called a big name.

clue.text: Objects to Ernest's replacement

indicators.note: replacement means putting in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive gives the letters as printed, including the final S

explanation.surface: Someone opposes the appointment of a substitute for Ernest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges all seven letters of ERNEST'S, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: To take exception to something is to feel bitter about it.

clue.text: Sign name in a dazed state

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the word for sign

parts.note: a trace is a sign or vestige

explanation.surface: Someone signs their name while half-asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb, but it is the noun TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a stupor or daze, a half-conscious condition.

clue.text: Mark the sailor is a six-footer

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor named Mark is unusually tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a sailor's name; 'six-footer' looks like a tall man but means an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: This sacred Egyptian beetle is an insect, and insects have six legs.

clue.text: More advanced as a teacher?

parts.note: a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if being a teacher means being further on.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the head is the head teacher, in charge of a school; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front means being further forward in progress.

clue.text: NEWSrooms

parts.note: the capitals pick out the four compass points North, East, West, South, the divisions of the compass, followed by a word for lodgings

explanation.walkthrough: N, E, W and S are the four points of the compass, each a quarter of it; rooms or lodgings are also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass points divide the horizon into fourths, and living accommodation is also known by the same word.

clue.text: Hothead raised the stake

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, which in a down answer reads a word from bottom to top

parts.note: Etna, a volcano in Sicily, is a mountain with a hot top

explanation.surface: An angry gambler upped the bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hothead' looks like an angry person but is the Sicilian volcano ETNA, which 'raised' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a poker player's stake put in before cards are dealt.

clue.text: Nevertheless, netting first and last service

parts.note: even so means nevertheless

indicators.note: first and last asks for the opening and closing letters of the word netting

explanation.surface: Despite everything, a footballer scores the opening and final goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' takes N and G from 'netting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is an evening church service in the Anglican tradition.

clue.text: Officer's quarters housing retired soldiers

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one piece is lodged within the other

parts.note: compass quarters give the letters E, N and N, points of the compass

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for soldiers is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer's lodgings take in soldiers who have left the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' gives compass points, here E, N and N; the reversal from 'retired' gives SIG, which 'housing' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned rank, historically the lowest officer in an infantry regiment.

clue.text: Compromise and put a stop to ill temper

parts.note: to end something is to put a stop to it
anger is ill temper

explanation.surface: Advice to settle differences and calm a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compromise' looks like the noun meaning a settlement, but it is the verb meaning to put at risk; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to put it in jeopardy, to expose it to risk.

clue.text: Condescends to change the design

indicators.note: to change the design is to alter its arrangement, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone graciously agrees to alter a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges DESIGN; 'to' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to stoop to doing something, thinking it beneath oneself.
